title: ID-JAG: a user's identity at an app whose IdP you do not control
lede: The exchange returns an identity assertion grant that the gateway redeems at the application's own issuer. No shared credential, no consent prompt. Ping release claim, UNVERIFIED on our tenant. Simulated.

edges.label: exchange for an ID-JAG, aud = partner issuer

steps.title: The agent calls the gateway
steps.what: The call carries the caller's token, from the IdP the gateway trusts.

steps.title: The gateway asks for a grant
steps.what: RFC 8693 exchange with a requested token type of an identity assertion grant.

steps.title: The IdP issues the grant
steps.what: A short-lived JWT naming the user and the partner issuer as its audience.

steps.title: The gateway redeems it at the app's issuer
steps.what: The grant is presented to the issuer the app trusts. No password, no secret of the user IdP.

steps.title: The partner issuer verifies the grant
steps.what: It trusts that IdP, set up in advance by an administrator, and checks signature, audience, expiry and that the grant was not used before.

steps.title: The partner issuer mints its own token
steps.what: The user's identity is now expressed in a token from the app's own issuer. No consent screen.

steps.title: The gateway calls the app
steps.what: The app validates its own issuer's token as usual.
